blocks.text: Substance Abuse in Our Country
Addiction in America

blocks.html: Addiction is a chronic disease that affects the brain and other body systems. Addiction to drugs or alcohol leads to an overwhelming need (compulsion) to use substances despite an awareness of their harmful effects. Addiction, whether to alcohol, opioids, or other illicit drugs, is responsible for various mental and medical health effects. They also lead to the loss of thousands of lives each year. Combined, addictions to illicit drugs, nicotine, and alcohol kill nearly 12 million people annually.

blocks.html: Although worldwide statics are shocking, the statistics about addiction and overdose close to home here in the US are equally as alarming. In the United States, up to 22 million Americans (some as young as age twelve) have at least one addiction. Unfortunately, less than 10% of those will ever seek or receive potentially lifesaving addiction treatment. Over half a million Americans of all ages and demographics have died from a drug overdose in the last decade. Also, more than 90% of those with a drug or alcohol use disorder today began experimenting with drugs or alcohol before turning eighteen.

Addiction in Southlake, Texas

blocks.html: The city of Southlake, located in Tarrant County, is home to approximately 32,000 people. Southlake and surrounding regions remained largely rural before the completion of the DFW International Airport in the 1970s, which led to a dramatic population increase that has continued over the last 40 years. The median household income in the Southlake area is around $240,000, with property values averaging over half a million dollars. Although medium incomes continue to rise, in Southlake, poverty rates continue to increase, with approximately 3% of the area population living below the poverty line.

blocks.html: Although smaller than neighboring cities such as Dallas, Southlake, and Tarrant county are not immune to many of the substance abuse challenges that impact larger cities and metropolitan areas. Rates of excessive drinking, overdose, and death related to drugs and alcohol remain high across Tarrant County. For example, in 2019, 19% of the adult population in the county reported either binge or heavy drinking. The Dallas-Fort Worth Healthcare Foundation reports indicate that between 2016 and 2018, the death rate for drug overdoses was 597 deaths per 100,000.

Data from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention shows in 2018, the opioid prescribing rate was 53.7 prescriptions per 100 people, or more than 50%. This led to more than 100 fatal overdoses in 2017 alone. In addition to the loss of life attributed to drug overdose, alcohol-impaired driving led to nearly 200 deaths between 2015 and 2019, accounting for more than 23% of all driving-related deaths during those years.

blocks.html: Addiction is a disease that affects everyone differently. While two people may share the same addiction, the symptoms they have while actively using drugs or drinking and the challenges they face while attempting to get sober will differ based on factors unique to the person. Therefore, a crucial element of successful addiction treatment is designing treatment programs based on the unique needs of the individual seeking help. This is achieved by providing a range of treatment models, including medically supported detox, evidence-based treatments, alternative therapies, and comprehensive aftercare planning.

Detoxification

blocks.html: Detoxification or detox is often the first step for many seeking lasting sobriety. Suppose you have an addiction to certain substances such as opioids, alcohol, or benzodiazepines. In that case, it is vital (and in most cases lifesaving) to seek treatment in a facility with a professional medical detox program. During medically supported detox, medical and mental health providers provide support and care throughout the stages of detox. This may include monitoring your physical health (vital signs, etc.) and administering medications to help reduce the intensity and severity of certain withdrawal symptoms.

Dual Diagnosis Treatment

blocks.html: Our dual diagnosis treatment center in Texas offers programs to address both the physical aspects and underlying psychological causes of addiction. It’s common for individuals with substance abuse issues to also have mental health problems or vice versa. Substance use can result from attempting to self-medicate for mental health symptoms, leading to chronic drug use and addiction. Without proper dual diagnosis care, the root issue remains unresolved and the risk of relapse is high.

Aftercare Support

blocks.html: Aftercare plans are tailored programs set up after primary addiction treatment to meet your ongoing support needs. A good aftercare plan should provide you with the necessary tools and guidance to successfully navigate daily life after treatment. SAMHSA (Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration) states that a successful aftercare plan supports long-term recovery through evidence-based practices and various support services to sustain sobriety.
